analysis:
All three changed files are test-only (ClusterOwnerServingTests.swift, ClusterPairServingDecisionsTests.swift, DistributedAutomaticBatchPlannerTests.swift). They ship no production code, and I found no new secrets, network surface, or auth path in them.

The tests exercise cluster owner-serving and public-traffic qualification behaviour that lives in other files not supplied here (ClusterPairServingGrants, ClusterPublicModels, ClusterPlacementTensorAssistantSelection, ClusterSetupPlanning). Security-relevant contracts the tests encode:
1. A model declared public (ClusterPublicModels) is qualified for public traffic in its declared families (pipeline and tensor parallel) without a record. This holds only for the declared artifact digest. A different artifact, an undeclared mode family (pipelineMTP, phaseSplit), or an undeclared model reports 'not yet qualified'.
2. Qwen's speculative assistant is never offered for public traffic (tensorAssistantNotOffered). Under the default auto mode, discoveryMode returns .off when the cluster is served through the coordinator.
3. Owner serving is distinct from public qualification. Diverged shapes are steered away from, and a model with no stage adapter is refused.

The test at ClusterOwnerServingTests.swift lines 72-109 pins that declaration alone qualifies the public line. The text says the coordinator's parity qualification still decides each placement. That coordinator-side gate is platform-owned and not visible here, so the next pass should confirm that the declaration in ClusterPublicModels, which is production code, cannot widen public grants beyond the declared artifact and families.

The onLargeStack helper in DistributedAutomaticBatchPlannerTests.swift (lines 1083-1097) uses @unchecked Sendable with a semaphore handoff. It is test-only and safe in practice.

No regression is identified in the supplied evidence. The production implementation of publicTrafficLine and ClusterPublicModels was not supplied, so I could not verify the production side of these contracts. This is a coverage limit, not evidence of safety.
